plan: Store the workspace as a single deep-copied dict tree and treat it as the sole source of truth; all queries and mutations operate on this tree.
Centralize traversal in one recursive generator that yields (item, depth) pairs so word counting, marker collection, and outlining share identical iteration order.

Dispatch per item kind: notes contribute regex-derived word counts and markers parsed from text; references contribute their declared word_count and unresolved list; sections/groups recurse into their items.
Isolate marker handling with a compiled regex for [[?identifier]] tokens: strip markers before counting words so marker syntax never counts, and capture identifiers for the unresolved set.

Implement move as validate-then-mutate: resolve the item with its parent list, resolve the destination container, and check id types, existence, container-ness, subtree containment, and index bounds before any list is touched, guaranteeing failed moves leave the tree unchanged.
Perform the mutation as pop-from-parent then append/insert into the destination list, which preserves the moved subtree by reference and only alters location/order.
Return deep copies from to_data() so callers can never mutate internal state.
mechanisms: deep-copy-on-ingest and deep-copy-on-export for state isolation
single recursive depth-tracking traversal shared by all read operations
kind-based dispatch for summary contributions (note vs reference vs container)
compiled marker regex with strip-before-word-count to exclude marker tokens
validate-then-mutate move protocol for atomicity on failure
subtree id scan to reject self/descendant containment
explicit insertion-index bounds check (0..len inclusive) with type guards
